title: Stalk surjectivity from a fixed connective rank-one affine representative
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $E\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $a:\mathcal O_S[0]\to E$, and $s\in S$. Suppose $U$ is an affine open containing $s$, $P$ is a strictly perfect complex on the localized site over $U$ [def-pc-perfect-complex], and $e:E|_U\simeq Q(P)$ is a specified derived isomorphism. Assume $P^i=0$ for every $i<0$ and $P^0\simeq\mathcal O_U$. Let $i_s$ denote the residue-field map [def-pc-base-change], with derived pullback as in [def-pc-derived-pullback]. If $H^0(Li_s^*a)$ is invertible, then the stalk map $H^0(a)_s$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is surjective. The model is supplied in the hypotheses; no construction of it or computation of Betti numbers is part of the conclusion.

proof.text: Construct the single complex A on the restricted structure sheaf. Its only nonzero term is free of rank one, using coproductUniqueIso, so A is strictly perfect. The exact restriction/single-functor comparison supplies c. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-map-representative] to c.inv followed by the restricted a and e.hom to obtain alpha with the representing equality.

Apply [lem-sc-rank-one-residue-stalk-component] to that actual representative. Its degree-zero additive stalk component is invertible, hence epic. The source degree-one term vanishes, so its outgoing differential vanishes. The chain-map equation and cancellation by the epic component force the target outgoing differential to vanish too. Both cycle inclusions are isomorphisms; naturality then makes the cycle map epic. ShortComplex.epi_homologyMap_of_epi_cyclesMap gives an epic degree-zero homology map.

By [lem-sc-localized-homology-stalk-comparison], the localized stalk functor is exact and restriction preserves homology stalks naturally. Compose its homology comparison with DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors. Naturality transports the epic homology map through Q; use the representing equality and cancel the isomorphisms c and e. Finally use the restriction-stalk natural isomorphism to transport epicness to the original homology stalk map. AddCommGrpCat.epi_iff_surjective gives the required surjectivity.

theorem surjective_stalk_homology_of_connective_rank_one_model (S : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : S.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [∀ x : S, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (moduleRings (Spec (S.residueField x)).toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory S)
    (a : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) ⟶ E) (s : S)
    (U : S.Opens) (hs : s ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (P : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hP : Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect S U P)
    (hnegative : ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero (P.X i))
    (hzero : Nonempty (P.X 0 ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))))
    (e : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
    (ha : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (S.residueField s)).toRingedSpace)) 0).map
        ((derivedPullback (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).map a))) :
    Function.Surjective (Scheme.Modules.Hom.stalkLinearMap
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0).map a) s)
